1-1.text: Part one. Four ways to move a shape. ... A transformation changes where a shape is, which way it faces, or how big it is.

1-2.text: There are four kinds. A reflection flips. A rotation turns. A translation slides. An enlargement makes a shape bigger or smaller.

1-3.text: After a reflection, rotation or translation, the new shape is exactly the same size and shape. We say it is congruent. Only an enlargement changes the size.

2-1.text: Part two. Reflection. ... A reflection flips a shape over a mirror line. Here the mirror line is the y-axis.

2-2.text: Every corner of the image is the same distance from the mirror line as the corner it came from, but on the other side. This corner is 4 squares from the line on each side.

2-3.text: Reflect the point 3, 2 in the y-axis and it goes to negative 3, 2. The x-coordinate changes sign. The y-coordinate stays the same.

2-4.text: Now the mirror line is the x-axis. The point 4, 3 goes to 4, negative 3. This time the y-coordinate changes sign.

3-1.text: Part three. Translation. ... A translation slides a shape. It does not turn or flip.

3-2.text: Every point moves the same distance in the same direction. Here each corner moves 5 squares right and 2 squares down.

3-3.text: With coordinates: moving right adds to x, left takes away from x. Up adds to y, down takes away from y. So 1, 2 moved 3 right and 2 up goes to 4, 4.

3-4.text: The image is congruent: the same size and shape, and it still faces the same way.

4-1.text: Part four. Rotation. ... A rotation turns a shape. A quarter turn is 90 degrees. A half turn is 180 degrees. A full turn is 360 degrees.

4-2.text: To describe a rotation, give three things: the angle, the direction (clockwise or anticlockwise) and the centre, the point it turns about.

4-3.text: This triangle turns 90 degrees clockwise about the origin, 0, 0. Every point turns around the centre by the same angle.

4-4.text: A half turn about the origin changes the sign of both coordinates. 3, 1 goes to negative 3, negative 1.

5-1.text: Part five. Enlargement. ... An enlargement changes the size. The scale factor tells you how many times bigger. With scale factor 3, a 2 by 1 rectangle becomes 6 by 3.

5-2.text: To find the scale factor, divide the new length by the old length. Here 6 divided by 2 equals 3. The angles stay the same.

5-3.text: An enlargement can have a centre. With scale factor 2, every corner ends up twice as far from the centre as before.

5-4.text: Watch out for area! With scale factor 2, the length and the width both double, so the area is 2 times 2, which is 4 times bigger.

6-1.text: Part six. Symmetry. ... A shape has line symmetry if you can fold it along a line and the two halves match exactly. That line is a line of symmetry.

6-2.text: An equilateral triangle has 3 lines of symmetry. A square has 4.

6-3.text: Rotational symmetry: turn the shape. Count how many times it fits onto itself in one full turn. A square fits 4 times, so its order is 4.

6-4.text: The letter S and a parallelogram both fit onto themselves after a half turn: order 2. A parallelogram has no lines of symmetry at all.
